columns.Year: calendar year of the trading record (integer, 1900-1920)
columns.Hare: snowshoe hare pelts traded by the Hudson's Bay Company, thousands of pelts
columns.Lynx: Canadian lynx pelts traded by the Hudson's Bay Company, thousands of pelts

units: thousands of pelts per year (values copied unchanged from the source)
observation_note: Fur-trade counts, not population censuses. Treat as abundance indices only; absolute population sizes cannot be inferred from them.

source.name: Stan case study data file hudson-bay-lynx-hare.csv
source.described_in: Carpenter, B. (2018). Predator-Prey Population Dynamics: the Lotka-Volterra model in Stan. https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/case-studies/lotka-volterra-predator-prey.html
lineage: Purves, Sadava, Orians and Heller, Life: The Science of Biology (textbook figure)
Mahaffy, J. M. (2010), Math 636 lecture notes, San Diego State University
Howard, P. (2009), Modeling Basics, Math 442 lecture notes, Texas A&M University (http://www.math.tamu.edu/~phoward/m442/modbasics.pdf)
Carpenter (2018) Stan case study CSV (this file)
source.transformations: Removed the two '#' comment lines, removed spaces after commas, reordered columns from Year,Lynx,Hare to Year,Hare,Lynx. No values changed.

cross_check.name: tsibbledata pelt (Hudson Bay Company trading records, 1845-1935)
cross_check.units: thousands of pelts in the CSV (the R package multiplies by 1000)

agreement_1900_1920.note: The two compilations differ substantially year by year, especially for hare. Not used for fitting; recorded so the choice of series is explicit.
